University Of Pennsylvania Receives $15 Million Commitment From Josh And Marjorie Harris
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:33 AM
University Of Pennsylvania Receives $15 Million Commitment From Josh And Marjorie Harris
Josh Harris and his wife, Marjorie Harris, have made a $15 million commitment to the University of Pennsylvania through Harris Philanthropies.
The commitment includes $10 million to establish the Harris Family Alternative Investments Center at the Wharton School and $5 million to renovate Penn Wrestling’s facilities and support the athletic program.
The gifts, announced during Josh Harris’ 40th Wharton reunion, bring the couple’s total support for the university to approximately $34 million. Their cumulative giving to Wharton’s alternative-investments programming now totals $25 million.
Expanding Alternative Investments Research
The $10 million Wharton gift will transform the Harris Alternative Investments Program into the Harris Family Alternative Investments Center.
Harris originally established the program in 2019 with a $10 million commitment. The new center will expand its work across student programming, faculty research and engagement with the global investment industry.
Its research will examine how private markets are evolving and how their growth affects institutions, investors and beneficiaries. The center also plans to translate academic findings into practical industry insights and policy recommendations.
The existing Wharton Alternative Investments Summit will become the Harris Family Alternative Investments Conference. The event will convene investment professionals, academics, alumni and students to discuss trends shaping private equity and other alternative asset classes.
Fellowships And Financial Data
Harris Student Fellows will receive stipends, funding for travel and invitations to center events. They will also gain access to affiliated faculty, guest speakers, industry executives and professional mentors.
The center will establish a dedicated data hub offering premium financial datasets to Wharton students, faculty members and researchers studying alternative investments and private markets.
The commitment also expands Harris’ previous support for the Wharton Private Equity Professorship, held by Bilge Yilmaz, and the Joshua J. Harris Professorship, held by Thomas S. Robertson.
Yilmaz and Burcu Esmer will serve as the center’s academic directors.
New Penn Wrestling Facilities
The Harrises’ $5 million athletics gift will support the renovation of Weightman Hall and the creation of the Pottruck-Reina Wrestling Center.
The 13,000-square-foot project will include the 8,900-square-foot Harris Family Wrestling Room, which will serve as the team’s main training space. A new 2,400-square-foot team complex will replace the adjacent Donaldson Room and provide athletes with modern locker rooms and related facilities.
The renovated center is expected to open in spring 2028.
Part of the gift will support the Grapplers Fund, which gives Penn Wrestling flexible resources for program operations. The commitment builds on Harris’ prior support for coaching, recruiting, team travel, nutrition and equipment.
Harris competed as a wrestler while attending Penn. The National Wrestling Hall of Fame recognized him as an Outstanding American in 2013.

Cosine Robots raises Rs 22.36 Cr led by Avaana Capital
Bengaluru-based deeptech startup Cosine Robots has raised Rs 22.36 crore ($2.4 million) in a funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH
Shashank Pathak
24 Nov 2026
10:13
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Bengaluru-based deeptech startup Cosine Robots has raised Rs 22.36 crore ($2.4 million) in a funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to set up a dedicated research and development (R&D) and production facility, expand its engineering team and accelerate the development of its integrated servo actuator portfolio.
Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas, Cosine Robots develops actuators and motion systems for robotics applications. Its products combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics and proprietary control software into integrated systems designed to control robotic movement.
The company is developing a common motion architecture through a modular range of cycloidal and planetary actuators. These products are designed for different torque requirements across industrial robotic arms, collaborative robots, quadrupeds and humanoid robots.
Cosine’s technology also includes a proprietary control architecture that combines dual-position sensing with a 25 kHz control loop, enabling 25,000 updates per second. The system is designed to improve precision and control over movement and torque.
The upcoming facility will bring precision machining, assembly, calibration and endurance testing under one roof. The company aims to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities and supply actuators to robot manufacturers in India and overseas.
Avaana Capital invests in deeptech and innovation-led businesses across sectors including advanced manufacturing, AI, robotics, mobility and climate technology. Its portfolio includes Eggoz, Tsuyo Manufacturing, Dreamfly and Kazam.

British-Ukrainian Pai Defence Raises €4.58M to Expand Drone Detection in Ukraine
Nordic VC fund Gardar led Pai Defence’s pre-seed round. The British-Ukrainian startup plans to expand its drone detection network in Ukraine and build on data from more than 100,000 flights it says it has tracked.
Defense Tech Pai Defence Ukraine News Deals
The Recursive
by
The Recursive
November 24, 2026 ∙ 1 min read
Share
Written by
The Recursive
Editor’s Choice
Fuckup Nights Sofia Vol. 4
Fintech Pulse 2026
What Good Is a Vested Option You Can’t Afford to Keep?
Pai Defence , a British-Ukrainian defense tech startup, has raised $5 million (€4.58 million) in pre-seed funding to expand its network of drone detection sensors in Ukraine and further develop its machine-learning software. Nordic venture capital fund Gardar led the round.
UA1, D3, Green Flag, Defence Builder, 1991 Ventures, Motanka, WildField, TA Ventures, and Angel One also participated.
Founded in 2025 by military volunteer and commander Dmytro and aerospace engineer Tonia Zakorchemna, Pai Defence is building a system to give Ukrainian military units a clearer picture of drone activity in crowded airspace. Its sensors detect radio signals from drones, and its software uses the data to identify drone types and analyze patterns across flights.
From individual alerts to a broader picture of drone activity
Ukraine has improved battlefield coordination through its Delta platform, but Pai Defence says much of the work of detecting drones still falls to individual operators. An alert can tell a unit that a drone is nearby. Pai’s aim is to bring those detections together so units can see how drone activity changes over time.
“For the most lethal weapon on the frontline, a detector’s beep when the drone is almost overhead is far too late,” said Zakorchemna, Pai Defence’s CEO and co-founder.
The company says it has tested its system in combat with Ukrainian military units and tracked more than 100,000 drone flights . It is using that data to refine its software as drone activity and tactics change.
“We believe Pai Defence has cracked the code for a major part of this problem, and that they can contribute to saving many lives on the frontlines,” said Erlend Prestgard, Gardar Managing Partner.
Pai Defence is headquartered in Ukraine and plans to grow its engineering team as it deploys more sensors along the front line . Its longer-term goal is to build a real-time map of drone activity.

China's Jindun Group Subsidiary Invests CNY 170 Million in Xihe Chuangxin to Secure Position in Advanced Computing Clusters
Add preferred source
China's Jindun Group announced that its 60%-owned subsidiary Hedian Xingdun will subscribe to CNY 680,000 of newly added registered capital in Xihe Chuangxin Artificial Intelligence Technology with CNY 170 million (approximately $25.5 million) in cash, acquiring a 41% stake. The capital increase is being undertaken jointly by Hedian Xingdun, Lunar Surface Exploration, MetaX Digital Intelligence and Jiliu Technology, with total funding of CNY 250 million (approximately $37.6 million) earmarked exclusively for investment, construction and operation of advanced computing clusters. Following the increase, Xihe Chuangxin's registered capital rises from CNY 1 million to CNY 2 million. MetaX Digital Intelligence, a wholly owned subsidiary of MetaX, holds 15%, creating an indirect capital link with Jindun Group. Jindun Group reported revenue of CNY 223 million (approximately $33.5 million) for the first three quarters, down 7.18% year-on-year, while net profit attributable to shareholders fell 72.37%, underscoring pressure on its core business as it pursues a transformation using its own and self-raised funds. The technical and market risks of entering the AI computing sector remain unverified.
Key Elements
Jindun Group Hedian Xingdun Intelligent Computing Xihe Chuangxin Artificial Intelligence Technology MetaX Digital Intelligence MetaX Lunar Surface Exploration Jiliu Technology Tupeng Shengyuan advanced computing clusters data center cooling
China's Jindun Group (300411.SZ) announced on November 23 that its 60%-owned subsidiary Hedian Xingdun Intelligent Computing (Shanghai) Technology Co. will subscribe to CNY 680,000 of newly added registered capital in Xihe Chuangxin Artificial Intelligence Technology (Shanghai) Co. with CNY 170 million (approximately $25.5 million) in cash, securing a 41% stake and becoming the largest shareholder of the advanced computing cluster platform.
The transaction is not a single-institution investment. Under a multi-party joint venture cooperation agreement on the computing industry signed by Hedian Xingdun together with Lunar Surface Exploration (Shanghai) Power Technology Co., MetaX Digital Intelligence (Shanghai) Technology Co., Shanghai Jiliu Technology Co. and Shanghai Tupeng Shengyuan Enterprise Management Partnership (limited partnership), the parties are injecting cash at a price of CNY 250 per CNY 1 of registered capital, for a total capital increase of CNY 250 million (approximately $37.6 million) and CNY 1 million in newly added registered capital. Of that, CNY 249 million (approximately $37.6 million) is booked as capital reserve, and Xihe Chuangxin's registered capital rises from CNY 1 million to CNY 2 million.
Following completion, Xihe Chuangxin's ownership structure will be: Hedian Xingdun 41%, Lunar Surface Exploration 33%, MetaX Digital Intelligence 15%, Jiliu Technology 6% and Tupeng Shengyuan 5%. Tupeng Shengyuan waived its preferential subscription right for this round and did not participate in the capital increase.
Notably, MetaX Digital Intelligence is a wholly owned subsidiary of MetaX, meaning Jindun Group and the GPU chip maker have formed an indirect capital link at the Xihe Chuangxin level.

Montréal Startup Secures Seed Capital to Innovate Insurance with AI Platform
November 24, 2026 by Knowlton Thomas Leave a Comment
A fintech startup based out of Québec has raised a seed round.
When an employee goes on leave, gets hurt on the job, or leaves the company, all sorts of different benefits insurers and providers need to be aware of the changes. This is where 8/0 comes in.
Montréal’s Eight by Zero Technologies , which has developed a universal interoperability platform for the insurance industry, has secured US$3 million.
Eight by Zero’s multi-tenant platform connects insurers, employers, and HR systems through APIs and file-based integrations for a streamlined approach.
“Carriers have rebuilt the same integration for every employer they onboard,” explains Sam Kasle, cofounder Eight by Zero. “We build it once, and the carrier can get it for every line it writes for that employer.”
The round was led by Diagram with participation from Canada Life.
Inside a large financial institution, “integration work quietly eats the roadmap, and insurers pay that cost again every time they onboard an employer,” according to Gaurav Kapoor, General Partner at Diagram.
“[Eight by Zero] does that work once and keeps it running, so carriers can put their people on claims and coverage,” he remarked.
Eight by Zero represents an “opportunity to create a more connected experience for our plan sponsors and advisors,” believes Julia McGillis, Executive Vice President of Workplace Benefits & Retirement at Canada Life.
“The capabilities developed by Eight by Zero will further accelerate investments we’re making in technology to simplify how data is connected across benefits and insurance, helping reduce integration complexity for employers and carriers,” she commented.
Proceeds from the seed round will fund product development, expansion into new lines of coverage, customer implementation capacity, and commercial growth, according to a statement from the Canadian fintech.
Eight by Zero was founded in 2025.
